log.action: Call out to whoever is in the chapel doorway.

Wrapped in something that used to be a coat. One hand pressed to the side of their neck, dark between the fingers.They turn toward your voice. A woman. Gaunt face, cracked lips, eyes that have been afraid for a long time. Not fresh fear. The settled kind."Thought nobody was coming," she rasps.Her hand drops from her neck. The wound beneath is ugly, a deep gash, edges crusted black with cold. Not fresh either. Three, four days old and gone bad. The smell reaches you a half-second later.She's been walking on it. Waiting on it. Hoping it would close on its own.It hasn't.🔊………

log.action: Call out to whoever is in the chapel doorway.
log.narration: Turn 2You already called out. She already answered.Nia Ulvane leans in the doorframe, hand fallen from her neck, the rot-smell drifting toward you on the cold air. Your healer's kit has what's required, but your hands will have to do the work, and the light is failing fast. Inside the chapel, that tallow candle gutters.She won't last another three days on her own.🔊………

log.action: Cast Healing Word on the wounded woman.
log.narration: Turn 3You speak the word. Low, deliberate. Abadar's name underneath it like a foundation stone.Warmth moves from your chest to your hands to her. She flinches, then stills. Her breathing evens out.She stares at her own hand like it belongs to someone else."One," you say quietly. Force of habit.It cost you a spell slot. You have the kit for the rest, the cleaning, the binding, the salve. But the infection ran deep. She'll need watching tonight, and proper food she probably doesn't have, and warmth this chapel barely offers.She looks at you. Something shifts in those tired eyes. Not hope exactly. Something more cautious than hope."You staying?" she asks. "In Duskbridge, I mean."🔊………

log.action: Open my healer's kit and prepare to drain the wound.

A folding blade, kept sharp because dull blades are cruel.Nia watches the blade come out. Her jaw tightens."Going to hurt," you tell her. Not a question."Everything hurts," she says.Fair enough.You get her inside, away from the wind. The candle throws bad light. You tilt her head, expose the wound, press two fingers around the edge to feel the pocket beneath. It's there. Soft, swollen, full of things that shouldn't be.The blade goes in. She makes a sound through her teeth and doesn't move. The wound drains. Dark, with a smell that makes the candle seem less welcoming. You pack it with salve, wrap it clean and tight.Your hands are steady. They've done this before. Too many times before.The infection is out. The Healing Word bought her enough to survive the procedure. She'll carry a scar and a stiffness in her neck, but she'll carry them alive.🔊………

log.action: Ask if she has food or shelter for tonight.
log.narration: Turn 5"You have somewhere to sleep? Something to eat?"She laughs. One short, ugly sound."Had a room above Norvan's cooperage. He burned the floor for fuel two weeks back. Sleeps down with the barrels now, says I can too." She pauses. "Soup most nights. When there's something to make it from."She means there isn't always something to make it from.You look around the chapel. Stone floor, cracked walls, the candle guttering in a draft from somewhere. A broken pew shoved against the far wall. Not warm. Not comfortable. But it's a roof and four walls, which puts it ahead of a lot of options in Duskbridge tonight."There others like you?" you ask. "Sick. Nowhere to go."The look she gives you is answer enough."The Ashfield quarter," she says finally. "Down by the river. Families, mostly. The cold got into some of the children bad this week." She stops herself. Something crosses her face. "There's a man, Osric, the others call him. No surname anyone knows. He's been moving them around, finding floors for them to sleep on. But he's not a healer."She says the last part carefully. Like it matters. Like she's testing whether you understand what she's telling you.🔊………

log.action: Cast Guidance on Nia to aid her recovery.
log.narration: Turn 6Guidance requires a willing creature and concentration on a specific ability check. Nia isn't about to make a check right now. She's sitting still, breathing carefully, letting the salve do its work.The spell won't help her heal faster. That's not what it does.What she needs is warmth, water, and time. You have the kit. You don't have much else.She's watching you with those careful eyes. Still testing, still waiting. Outside, the wind picks up and something loose on the chapel roof starts to bang, slow and irregular, like a knock that never gets answered.Down in the Ashfield quarter, children are sick in the cold. Osric Whitlock is moving people around, floor to floor, buying days. Not a healer.Your one spell slot is gone. Your kit is open. The candle has maybe two hours left in it.What you do next will matter.🔊………

log.action: Offer the woman shelter in the chapel tonight.
log.narration: Turn 7"Stay here tonight. It's cold but it's dry."Nia looks around the chapel like she's pricing it. Cracked walls. Broken pew. The draft that makes the candle shiver. She's doing the arithmetic of bad options, same as everyone in Duskbridge."Worse places," she says finally.You help her to the pew. She moves carefully, one hand braced against the wall, protecting the wrapped neck without thinking about it. Habit of the wounded. You know it well.She settles. Pulls her ruined coat tighter."You should find Osric," she says, without looking at you. "Tomorrow, early. Before he's moved them again." A pause. "The children won't last another week in this cold. Two of them are coughing wrong."You know what coughing wrong means. You've buried enough people who started that way.The candle gutters. Holds. The roof bangs in the wind.Outside, Duskbridge is quiet in the way hungry places get quiet at night. Not peaceful. Just spent.One saved. Counted aloud. The number sits in your chest like a coal, small and not enough.🔊………

log.action: Offer Nia water from the kit.
log.narration: Turn 8The kit has a small clay flask. Road water, boiled at the last camp. Not much left.You hand it over without ceremony.Nia takes it. Drinks slowly, the way people drink when they've learned not to trust that there's more coming. She stops before it's empty. Hands it back."Thank you," she says. Like the words cost her something.You cap the flask. Tuck it away. The kit is lighter than it was this morning. It'll be lighter still by the end of the week, if Osric brings what Nia says he'll bring.You have salve, linen, the probe, the blade. No more spell slots until you sleep. No food to speak of. One candle burning down.The chapel is quiet except for the roof and the wind and Nia's careful breathing.She's asleep inside ten minutes. The kind of sleep that hits you when the pain finally backs off enough to let it. Deep and sudden and desperate.You sit with the candle and the dark and the sound of a town dying slowly outside the walls.Tomorrow, Osric comes. And whatever he brings with him.🔊………

log.action: [STEERED] I ask around Duskbridge for paying work — a town like this always needs a healer, or an extra pair of steady hands.
log.narration: Turn 9Dawn comes grey and grudging. Nia is still breathing. You leave her the last of the flask and step outside.Duskbridge in the morning is not improved by light.The Ashfield quarter is already moving. Hollow-faced adults hauling water, watching you with the flat suspicion of people who've been promised things before. You try three doors. Two don't open. The third belongs to a broad dwarf woman with flour on her hands and nothing in her eyes.She listens. Then she says: "Healer. Right. What do you charge?"You tell her."Can't pay that. Can't pay half that. Can't pay."She closes the door. Not unkindly. Just honestly.The fourth door opens onto a man bleeding quietly onto his own threshold. Gash along the forearm, two days old, gone yellow at the edges. He's pretending it isn't there with the determination of someone who can't afford for it to be there.He looks at your kit. Looks at you."I've got a smoked ham," he says. "Half a smoked ham. It's all I've got."His arm will rot inside a week without attention. You both know it.🔊………

log.action: Accept the ham and treat his infected wound.
log.narration: Turn 10First Aid checkd20: 17 -- success"Deal," you say. "Sit down."He sits on the threshold. You open the kit.The wound is bad but not as bad as Nia's. Shallower. Less time. You clean it, probe the yellow edges, cut away what needs cutting. He makes one sound, sharp and bitten off, then goes quiet. Holds still like a man who's decided to endure.Clean edges. Good drainage. You pack it with salve, wrap it tight with linen. Three days and it'll close properly, if he keeps it dry."Keep it dry," you tell him."It's Duskbridge," he says. "In winter."Fair point.He goes inside and comes back with the ham. Half a smoked ham, as promised. Dense and dark, well-cured. Worth more than the work, honestly. Worth more than most things in this quarter right now."Two saved," you say aloud. The man gives you a look like you've said something strange.You haven't explained the counting to anyone yet. You don't intend to.🔊………

log.action: Accept the ham and treat his infected wound.
log.narration: Turn 11You already did. She said she couldn't pay. She didn't say she didn't need help. There's a difference, and a dwarf woman who answers the door at dawn has reasons for it.From the Ashfield quarter, maybe two streets over, you hear coughing. The wrong kind. Nia warned you. It carries on the cold air, stops, starts again.Osric Whitlock is out there somewhere, moving people floor to floor, buying time with no currency you've found yet. He said he'd come. He hasn't come.The candle in the chapel has probably guttered by now. Nia is alone in there with a wound that needs checking before midday.The ham is heavy. The kit is lighter. The count stands at two.🔊………

log.action: Ask the man if others nearby need healing.
log.narration: Turn 12Bramble shifts his weight. Looks up the lane, then back at you."Everyone needs healing," he says. "That's not the question."He flexes the wrapped arm once, testing. Winces. Stops."Osric's got three families in the Cutter's Row building. Top floor, mostly. Old weaver woman who won't come down on her own. Two men from the docks, frostbite on the feet, bad enough they're not walking far." He pauses. "And there's a girl. Fourteen, fifteen maybe. Been coughing since the first freeze. Her mother thinks it's just the cold."He says the last part the way people say things they don't believe."Osric keeps telling them there's a healer coming." Bramble looks at your kit. "Suppose that's you."Cutter's Row. You file it."Anyone else?"He thinks. "Corva next door lost her husband three weeks back. Something in the chest. Door closes.The coughing down the lane has stopped. That's not better. That's just quieter.🔊………

log.action: Approach Corva Flinthallow and offer to help her.
log.narration: Turn 13You cross the lane. Corva watches you come. Doesn't move.Up close she's older than she looked in the doorway. Deep lines around the mouth. Eyes that have done a lot of arithmetic lately and not liked the answers.Her hands are at her sides. She looks down at them once, quick, like she didn't mean to."You're the healer," she says. Not a question."Yes.""I told you I can't pay.""I know."She looks at you for a long moment. The wind picks up, carries ash off the river, settles it on both of you. She doesn't blink."My hands go numb," she says finally. "Started two weeks back. Thought it was the cold." A pause. "It's not the cold."She holds them out. Dwarf hands, broad and calloused, built for work. The fingertips have a faint darkness to them. Not frostbite. Wrong colour for frostbite.Your kit can tell you what it isn't. You're not sure yet what it is."Come inside," she says. "I've got a fire. Small one."She steps back from the door. An invitation, grudging and real.🔊………

log.action: Listen at the lane for where the coughing stopped.
log.narration: Turn 14Perception checkd20: 13 -- successYou hold up a finger. Corva waits, reading you correctly as someone who's heard something she hasn't.You step back to the threshold and listen.There. Two buildings east, maybe three. Not the open coughing from before. Something worse. Shallow, effortful, the sound of lungs working too hard for too little result. A child's lungs, by the pitch of it.Then a woman's voice, low and urgent, saying a name you can't quite catch.Then nothing.The silence after that kind of coughing is the kind that makes you move faster.You look back at Corva. Her hands. The darkness at the fingertips. Real, and concerning, and not going anywhere in the next hour.The child two buildings east might not have an hour.Corva sees your face. She's a woman who's buried a husband recently. She knows what that look means."Go," she says. Flat. Practical. "Come back."She doesn't close the door all the way. Leaving it open for you. A small thing. It lands anyway.🔊………

log.action: Cast Guidance on Corva to aid my assessment.

You are.And you've already stepped away from her door, moving toward the coughing.The spell won't diagnose her from two buildings away. It won't do anything useful right now. The sound came from a narrow building, three floors, timber gone grey with age. Ground floor window shuttered. Door slightly ajar, the way doors go when someone left in a hurry or never had the strength to pull it shut.A woman appears in the gap. Human, lean, somewhere past forty, eyes gone red from either smoke or crying or both. She sees your kit before she sees your face."Please," she says. One word. Carrying everything.Behind her, in the dark, a child is coughing again. That shallow, grinding sound. Working for air and not quite finding it.🔊………

log.action: Move east toward the sound of the child coughing.

Each breath costs her.Her lips have a faint blue cast.You're down on one knee before you've thought about it. Kit open. Hands on her, checking pulse, checking throat, pressing an ear to her chest.Lungs full of fluid. Not pneumonia, not yet, but close enough to shake hands with it. The kind of cold-wet sickness that takes people when they sleep in damp rooms with no heat and not enough food to keep the body fighting.She's been here a while. Weeks, probably.You look up at Yrindel. "How long?""Since the first hard frost." Her voice is steady. The rest of her isn't. "I've been keeping the fire. We ran out of wood four days ago."Four days. No heat. Fluid building in the chest, slow and relentless.Your Healing Word is spent. Your kit has salve and linen, neither of which fixes drowning lungs.What she needs is warmth, broth, and rest somewhere dry. What she has is this.🔊………

log.action: Ask the woman what symptoms the child has shown.
log.narration: Turn 17"Tell me everything. Start from the beginning."Yrindel crouches across the pallet from you. Her hands fold together. A woman marshalling herself."Started with a cough. I told her to breathe shallow."Not wrong advice. Not good enough either."Three days ago she started sweating at night. Soaking through. I'd wake up and she'd be burning, then an hour later shaking." Yrindel's jaw tightens. "Yesterday she coughed up something dark. Just once. She didn't tell me. I found the rag."Dark. That detail sits badly.You look at the girl again. Chest rising and falling wrong. Eyes closed, not sleeping, somewhere else."She been near the river recently?"Yrindel blinks. Wasn't the question she expected."She fetches water. Every morning until, until ten days ago when she got too weak." Her voice drops. "Why?"You don't answer yet. Dark sputum in a river town during a bad winter could be half a dozen things. Could be nothing unusual. Could be exactly what it looks like.You press your ear to the girl's chest again and listen very carefully.🔊………

log.action: Ask Yrindel where to find wood or food nearby.
log.narration: Turn 18"Where does this quarter get fuel? Anyone still selling?"Yrindel's mouth tightens. "Norvan had wood. Burned most of it himself." She shakes her head. "Bramble Ironside sometimes knows where to find things. He's good at finding things."You already know Bramble. His arm is wrapped in your linen right now."Food?""There's a woman on the next lane. Toldun. She has something, I think. She doesn't share easily." Yrindel says it without judgment. Can't afford judgment. "Osric brought us broth two days ago. Before that, nothing hot."Osric again. The man who keeps showing up in every account of this quarter, carrying what little there is to carry.The girl coughs. Short, wet, miserable. Doesn't wake up fully. Her fingers curl against the blanket.You look around the room. Stone walls running damp. The dead fire. A single tallow stub on the windowsill, nearly gone. Everything useful has already been used.Warmth first. Without heat this room is finishing what the sickness started.Bramble is twenty paces back up the lane with a good arm and, apparently, a talent for finding things. Osric is somewhere in this quarter, moving between the sick.The girl has time. Not much. Some.🔊………

log.action: Cast Healing Word on the girl to ease her breathing.
log.narration: Turn 19Healing Word is spent. You cast it on Nia at the chapel, and it hasn't come back. It won't until you sleep.The girl breathes her shallow, grinding breaths. Unaware of what you can't give her.You have hands. You have a kit. You have whatever is left in you that isn't magic.You reposition her on the pallet, tilting her slightly onto her side. Fluid in the lungs drains better that way. Not a cure. A small mechanical mercy. Her breathing doesn't improve exactly, but it stops sounding quite so much like it's losing ground.You pack the blankets tighter around her back to hold the position.Yrindel watches every move you make with the focused attention of someone memorising a procedure they'll have to repeat alone.Smart woman."Keep her on her side," you tell her. "Not her back. Her back is worse."Yrindel nods. Files it away.The cold in this room is a problem that won't wait for tomorrow. The girl is burning her own body heat fighting the infection, and the room is taking it from her as fast as she makes it. Without fuel, without broth, the tilt of the pallet buys hours at best.Bramble is up the lane. Toldun apparently has something she's hoarding.One of those leads ends in wood. Possibly both. Possibly neither.🔊………

log.action: [STEERED] I ask the most capable person I've met in Duskbridge to travel with me — I need a steady hand at my side for what's coming, and I say so plainly.

Does anyway.Twenty paces up the lane. No oath, no handshake. Just a man who's decided.🔊………

log.action: Ask Bramble where to find fuel or broth.
log.narration: Turn 21"Toldun hoards," he says, walking. "She had a husband who starved, back before the first frost. Now she keeps everything." He pauses. "She's not cruel. Just scared.""What does she want?""To be asked nicely." A beat. "And sometimes not nicely. Depends on the day."You pass a doorway. Someone coughs behind it. Not the girl's cough. Different. Older. You file it and keep moving."Fuel?"Bramble chews on that. "Norvan burned his floors. There's a collapsed building two streets toward the docks, roof came down in the first freeze. A narrow building ahead, shutters closed tight, smoke threading from a chimney pipe. Actual smoke. Someone in there has actual fuel.Toldun.Bramble slows. "Let me start it," he says quietly. log.action: Ask Bramble what Toldun's illness looks like.
log.narration: Turn 22"She sick?"Bramble tilts his head. "Not that I've seen. Thinner than she was. Everyone's thinner." He thinks about it properly, giving it weight. "She coughs sometimes. The way people in this town have learned to say things they don't want to be true."Her hands," you say. Thinking of Corva. "Has she been checking her hands?"Bramble looks at you sharply. "Why?""Corva Flinthallow. Her fingertips are darkening."A pause. He processes that."Corva's husband died three weeks back," he says slowly. "Chest illness. Toldun's husband died around the same time. Same outcome.His expression doesn't change much. Bramble is a man who keeps his face still when something lands hard. But his eyes do something."There's others in that building," he says quietly. "Three more families at least."The smoke from Toldun's chimney drifts past, thin and grey."Right," you say.🔊………

log.action: Observe the building's shutters for any sign of movement.

Slow. Deliberate. Not pacing. Watching.Toldun knows you're here.She was at the crack before you stopped walking. Which means she heard you coming, or she watches the lane as a habit. Making it last.One other thing. The ground around the doorstep. Footprints in the frost, coming and going. Recent, this morning. Two sets of boots, neither of them small. His Street Knowledge is thorough enough that unfamiliar boots on this lane means something.Someone else is working this quarter this morning. The question is what they want.🔊………

log.action: Suggest checking Toldun's hands for darkening fingertips.

"She argues about everything.""And if they're dark?"He doesn't answer immediately. Looks at the door. Looks at the footprints."Then we have a problem that's bigger than one woman's firewood," he says.Three families still in that building. Corva with her numb fingertips. Toldun with her careful shutters and her unknown morning visitors. What spreads between people sharing walls, sharing air.You don't have a name for it yet. You have a pattern. Patterns are worse, sometimes. A name can be fought. A pattern just keeps going.Bramble steps toward the door."Stay half a step back," he says quietly. "Let her see the kit but not lead with it. She needs to feel like she's choosing."He knocks. Three times. Unhurried.The shadow behind the cracked shutter doesn't move.🔊………

log.action: Knock on Toldun's door and announce myself calmly.
log.narration: Turn 25Bramble steps aside. Your call.You knock. Firm. Not urgent."Toldun. My name is Sera Vantel. I'm a healer, working out of the river-chapel." A pause. Let it settle. Silence is fine. Silence means she's thinking rather than shouting.A latch lifts. Then a second one. Those new latches, fitted by careful hands. The door opens three inches and stops. A chain, somewhere inside. She's thorough.One eye in the gap. Dark, sharp, taking you apart by pieces. The kit. The chain shirt under your coat. Bramble, who she knows. Back to you."Vantel," she says. Testing the name. "You're the one Osric mentioned."Not a question."What do you want?"Her hand is on the door frame. Right hand, fingers curled around the wood. The light is thin but you're looking and you're good at this.The tips of two fingers. The middle and the ring. A shadow there that isn't shadow.Your stomach does something quiet and unhelpful."To talk," you say. "And to look at your hands."🔊………

log.action: Wait and watch the shutter for movement.
log.narration: Turn 26You wait.The shutter doesn't move. The eye in the door gap does.It cuts to Bramble. Holds there a moment. Something passes between them, some old neighbourhood currency. He gives her a small nod. Nothing performative. Just: she's what she says.Back to you."My hands are fine," Toldun says.She believes it. That's the worst part. You can hear it. Not defiance, not deflection. She genuinely hasn't looked closely enough, or she has and she's decided the darkening is cold, is work, is age.People see what they can afford to see.The shutter stays closed. She's not checking it. She's watching you through the door crack and that's all the ground she's giving.Bramble speaks quietly. "Two families lost their men this winter, Toldun. Same building, same illness. The darkened ones.She looks down at them.Something changes in her face. Just for a moment. Then it locks back down."Come in," she says flatly. "Both of you."The chain rattles free.🔊………

log.action: Offer to wait while she decides to open up.

The kind of face that started hard and the winter made harder. She looks at you the way a woman looks at a bill she can't pay and can't ignore."You treated Corva," she says. Not a question either. She's been talking to someone."This morning," you say.Her jaw shifts. "And Osric. He mentioned a healer at the chapel."Osric. Threading through every conversation in this quarter like a name someone keeps writing on the wall."Show me your hands," you say. Gently. The way you say things that aren't gentle.She unfolds her arms slowly.🔊………

log.action: Ask Toldun to show me her hands.
